name: Asymptotic Net
desc: Traces both families of asymptotic curves (zero normal curvature) for gridshell design. Asymptotic curves only exist where Gaussian curvature is negative; with AutoSpace the whole anticlastic region is filled with evenly spaced curves grown from one seed.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Seeds
inputs.desc: Seed vertex indices (optional with AutoSpace: the first one starts the net)

inputs.name: Step
inputs.desc: Integration step (0 = automatic: Spacing / 10, or from the mesh edge length)

inputs.name: MaxSteps
inputs.desc: Maximum steps per curve half (0 = automatic from the mesh size)

inputs.name: AutoSpace
inputs.desc: Fill the anticlastic region with evenly-spaced curves instead of tracing only from seeds

inputs.name: Spacing
inputs.desc: Target distance between adjacent curves (AutoSpace; 0 = automatic, bounding box / 30)

inputs.name: SeedPoints
inputs.desc: Seed points (nearest vertex is used); may be combined with Seeds

inputs.name: MaxCurves
inputs.desc: Cap on curves per family (AutoSpace, default 200)

inputs.name: Continuous
inputs.desc: Continuous curves: run to the border even where they come closer than Spacing to a neighbour; only near-coincident traces stop, ending on the neighbour. False stops traces at 0.4 x Spacing for a more even but interrupted layout

inputs.name: MinAngle
inputs.desc: Minimum crossing angle between the two families (degrees). Near the K = 0 line the families collapse onto each other; vertices below this angle are left out of the net and of the Anticlastic mask (default 15, 0 = raw K < 0 region)

inputs.name: Layout
inputs.desc: Layout of the family: 0 = evenly spaced fill (curves inserted and stopped to keep the spacing; T-junctions), 1 = web from the border (every curve border to border, seeds every Spacing along the border), 2 = web from the seed cross (seeds along the crossing curve through the seed), 3 = farthest-point fill (each new curve starts in the middle of the widest gap left, Mebarki et al. 2005: no gap wider than 1.6 x Spacing, fewer T-junctions, gaps less uniform than 0). Webs never merge; their spacing away from the seed line is what the surface dictates

outputs.name: FamilyA
outputs.desc: Right-handed asymptotic family (geodesic torsion +√−K)

outputs.name: FamilyB
outputs.desc: Left-handed asymptotic family (geodesic torsion −√−K)

outputs.name: Anticlastic
outputs.desc: Per input vertex: true where asymptotic directions exist (K < 0)

outputs.name: Net
outputs.desc: The whole net in one wire (surface + both families): plug it into Net Joints, Net Topology, Lath Sweep, Lath Analysis, Gridshell Analysis, Lath Segment, Lath Unroll, Lath Labels or Net Kinetics; Mite Net adds a profile and reports the lath ends

name: Asymptotic Web
desc: Schling's asymptotic web: nodes every Spacing along the two asymptotic curves through the seed, every other node the crossing of the curves through them — a quad net with no stubs and no T-junctions that keeps the surface's symmetry. A seed on a flat point (3-fold Enneper, monkey saddle) becomes a singular node where 2n rays meet; a surface of revolution gets the rotational web whose meridian diagonals are geodesics (an AAG web). With AAG on, the web is optimised so that one family of node diagonals is geodesic and every node star stays planar: three families of straight, flat slats (two upright, one lying on the surface).

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Surface mesh (negatively curved where the web should run)

inputs.name: Seed
inputs.desc: Seed point (optional: the mesh point nearest the bounding-box centre; a symmetric surface's centre)

inputs.name: Spacing
inputs.desc: Node distance along the two curves through the seed (0 = 4 % of the mesh diagonal)

inputs.name: Symmetry
inputs.desc: −1 = detect a rotation about the seed normal or a surface of revolution, 0 = none, n = force n-fold

inputs.name: AAG
inputs.desc: Optimise into an AAG web (geodesic diagonals, planar node stars); the surface moves slightly

inputs.name: Iterations
inputs.desc: AAG optimisation iterations

inputs.name: Proximity
inputs.desc: AAG: weight of staying on the reference surface (0 lets it float)

inputs.name: Diagonal
inputs.desc: Which diagonal family becomes geodesic: 0 = the straighter one, 1 = the other

inputs.name: Refine
inputs.desc: AAG: smooth laths through the joints (Schling, Wang, Hoyer & Pottmann 2022, §3.4). Every web edge is split into 2^Refine pieces and the fine net re-optimised so the refined laths stay asymptotic (upright) or geodesic (flat) while the joints stay put. 0 = off (laths are joint-to-joint chords), 1 = halves, 2 = quarters (the paper's choice, about five times slower)

outputs.name: A
outputs.desc: Asymptotic laths of the first family (upright strips)

outputs.name: B
outputs.desc: Asymptotic laths of the second family (upright strips)

outputs.name: G
outputs.desc: Node diagonals of the geodesic family (flat strips); with AAG off, the geodesic candidates

outputs.name: Nodes
outputs.desc: Web nodes (every A × B crossing)

outputs.name: Quads
outputs.desc: The web as a quad mesh on its nodes

outputs.name: Report
outputs.desc: Rays, symmetry, node count, diagonal geodesic error and — with AAG — star and geodesic errors and how far the surface moved

outputs.name: Surface
outputs.desc: AAG with Refine > 0: the refined quad mesh the smooth laths lie on (cladding, strip normals)

name: Chebyshev Net
desc: Constructs a Chebyshev net: equal edge lengths in both families everywhere. This is the kinematics of an elastic gridshell — a flat lattice of constant-length laths with rotating joints, bent into shape. Axis curves are geodesics from the seed; interior nodes are placed by the compass method (the surface point one edge length from both parents, solved to round-off). Hazzidakis: the shear angle falls with the curvature enclosed, so on domes the net locks away from the seed; MinAngle stops it before the laths touch.

inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.desc: Seed vertex index (net origin)

inputs.name: Direction

inputs.name: EdgeLength
inputs.desc: Lath segment length between joints

inputs.name: CountU
inputs.desc: Nodes per side of the seed, first family (default 10)

inputs.name: CountV
inputs.desc: Nodes per side of the seed, second family (default 10)

inputs.name: Angle
inputs.desc: Angle between families at the seed (default 90 degrees)

inputs.name: SeedPoint
inputs.desc: Net origin as a point (overrides Seed; nearest vertex is used)

inputs.name: MinAngle
inputs.desc: Smallest crossing angle allowed between the two families (0 = unlimited). A node whose cell would shear below it, or above 180° minus it, is not placed, so the net stops where the laths would lock. Garg et al. 2014 use 30° for wire meshes; try 20–30° for timber laths.

outputs.desc: Net nodes, one branch per row

outputs.name: UCurves
outputs.desc: Laths of the first family

outputs.name: VCurves
outputs.desc: Laths of the second family

outputs.name: NetMesh
outputs.desc: Quad mesh over the valid net cells

outputs.name: Angles
outputs.desc: Shear angle between the families at each node (degrees); locking occurs near 0 / 180

name: Dynamic Relaxation
desc: Form finding by dynamic relaxation with kinetic damping (Barnes 1999): the mesh edges act as springs, optionally under gravity / point loads, soap-film tension and smoothing, and the system is integrated until it rests in equilibrium. Hanging models, pre-tensioned cable nets, quick minimal-surface-like relaxations of a gridshell mesh, and with Bending > 0 an elastic gridshell whose laths are the rows and columns of the quad mesh.

inputs.desc: Rest length factor: 1 keeps edge lengths, < 1 pre-tensions the net (default 1)

name: Flat Kit
desc: Cut, assemble flat, deploy: presses an asymptotic net flat as a scissor mechanism (Net Kinetics' Flatten) and turns the flat state into a kit. Every lath becomes one straight strip with its joints at their spacing — the length the scissor joints keep through the whole motion — so the strips fit the flat grid and the curved one alike. Crossings of upright laths are halving slots (A from the outer edge, B from the inner edge, as wide as the other strip at the smallest angle the joint reaches), crossings of flat strips pin holes, and a node of three or more laths (the flat point of a 3-fold Enneper web) a hub. Outputs the flat assembly (joints numbered, laths labelled), the strips laid out on sheets, the deployment states, a cut list, and — with Write — SVG (red cut, blue engrave), DXF and CSV files in millimetres.

name: Geodesic Net
desc: Traces straightest geodesics from seeds along given directions for gridshell design. Geodesics extend both ways from each seed; with AutoSpace one family fills the mesh with evenly spaced geodesics grown from the first seed and direction. Each new geodesic starts at the angle that keeps the strip to its neighbour closest to constant width (Jacobi field, Pottmann et al. 2010), or the family leaves a border edge (FromBorder).

inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Seeds
inputs.desc: Seed vertex indices

inputs.name: Directions
inputs.desc: Initial direction per seed (last reused if fewer)

inputs.desc: Continuous curves: run to the border even where they come closer than Spacing to a neighbour; only near-coincident traces stop, ending on the neighbour. False stops traces at 0.4 x Spacing for a more even but interrupted layout

inputs.name: FromBorder
inputs.desc: AutoSpace: start the family on the border edge nearest the first seed (geodesics leave it every Spacing at BorderAngle from the inward normal) instead of growing sideways from the seed alone. Good on vaults and long patches; ignored on closed meshes

inputs.name: BorderAngle
inputs.desc: FromBorder: angle in degrees between the border geodesics and the inward normal of the border (0 = perpendicular to the edge)

inputs.name: Layout
inputs.desc: Layout of the family: 0 = evenly spaced fill (new geodesics beside existing ones, stopped where they converge; T-junctions), 1 = web from the border edge nearest the seed (every geodesic runs until it leaves the mesh, seeds every Spacing along the edge at BorderAngle), 2 = web from the seed cross (seeds every Spacing along the geodesic through the seed perpendicular to Direction, each parallel-transported). Webs never merge; geodesics converge where K > 0 and diverge where K < 0 (Jacobi), so their spacing away from the seed line is what the surface dictates

desc: Shortest path on a mesh between two points: the straight lath you would lay from A to B. Method 1 (default) gives the exact geodesic of the mesh by edge flips (FlipOut, Sharp & Crane 2020): straight across every face and edge, never through a cone tip, through a saddle vertex only when that is shorter. Method 0 is the older curve shortening. Points are matched pairwise (the last is reused when lists differ).

inputs.name: From

inputs.name: Method

name: Gridshell Analysis
desc: Linear static analysis of a lath network as a 3D beam frame. Laths become Euler-Bernoulli beams with the strip section, coupled at net crossings (rigid, scissor hinge or semi-rigid about the surface normal); supports are fixed or pinned points; loads per metre of lath, self-weight, area load and point loads. Geometry is converted from the document units to metres internally, so E / Allowable are in Pa and Load in N/m whatever the model units. A first-order sanity check, not a full FE package.

name: Net Kinetics

name: Net Kinetics
desc: Moves a scissor-jointed asymptotic net as a mechanism (Wan, Crolla & Schling 2025; Schikore et al. 2020). The crossings of A and B become scissor hinges: the distance between consecutive joints along every lath stays constant, every lath segment stays perpendicular to the (moving) surface normal at its ends — so upright laths remain straight-unrollable — and laths keep their rest bend with the given Stiffness. Drive the motion with Fixed points, Slide points (joints kept on the ground plane, free to slide), points moved To targets, Cables whose Lengths change, or Flatten (press the net onto a plane); Fold 0…1 runs the drivers from the rest state to the target in Steps states. Drift, Deviation and Miss tell you how well the mechanism can follow (a rigid net cannot follow at all; the exact doubly ruled grids follow to 1e-12). Every state is also read elastically (Schikore, Schling, Oberbichler & Bauer 2020): bending and twist strains of the lath section (Upright/Width/Thickness or Shape/Section, as Lath Analysis), the strain energy Π = ½∫(GJτ² + EIκ²) ds per state and the natural (least-energy) state along the motion.

name: AGG Web
desc: Asymptotic–geodesic–geodesic web (Schling, Wang, Hoyer & Pottmann 2022): takes a quad net of two lath families (Geodesic Net, Asymptotic Web, or your own curves crossing once per node) and moves its nodes so that both families are geodesic — equal opposite angles at every node, Sauer's condition — and one family of node diagonals is asymptotic (its edges in the tangent plane the laths define), while staying close to the surface. Two families of flat slats on the surface and one of upright slats. Exact on a developable surface with the rulings as diagonals (the cylinder web of the paper); elsewhere the surface moves a little and the report says how much.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Reference surface mesh the web stays close to

inputs.name: A
inputs.desc: Laths of the first family (each crossing every B lath at most once)

inputs.name: B
inputs.desc: Laths of the second family

inputs.name: Family
inputs.desc: Which diagonal family becomes asymptotic: −1 = the one lying nearer the surface's tangent planes at the start, 0 or 1

inputs.name: Iterations
inputs.desc: Gauss–Newton iterations (the last third without fairness)

inputs.name: Proximity
inputs.desc: Weight of staying on the reference surface (0 lets the web float)

inputs.name: Fairness
inputs.desc: Fairness weight along the three families (second differences)

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.desc: Largest gap accepted as a crossing (0 = 5 % of the sampling step)

inputs.name: Sampling
inputs.desc: Chord length for sampling the input curves (0 = bounding box / 500)

outputs.name: A
outputs.desc: Geodesic laths of the first family, node to node (flat slats)

outputs.name: B
outputs.desc: Geodesic laths of the second family (flat slats)

outputs.name: Diagonals

outputs.name: Other

outputs.name: Normals

outputs.name: Quads

outputs.name: Geodesic

outputs.name: Asymptotic

outputs.name: Deviation
